title: Delegated Erase Wizard with Certified Summary Export
creator: June Park
description:
Problem: Customers operating across regions and multiple retention policies need a simple, auditable way to request and confirm tenant-scoped erasures without escalating to support. Existing delete flows are internal-only and produce siloed logs that are hard to reconcile for customers and auditors.

Proposal: Build a Delegated Erase Wizard in the Console + an accompanying API that: 1) lets tenant admins submit scoped erasure requests (by data class, date range, and region), 2) runs a deterministic multi-step purge pipeline (soft-delete -> async expunge -> replica sweep -> index rebuild), and 3) emits a cryptographic-certified summary (signed hashchain + human-readable report) that customers can download or receive via webhook. The export should include provenance (which services/hosts touched the data), timestamps, and a machine-verifiable hash linked to an audit ledger.

Goals:
- Reduce manual support tickets for RTBF by 80% for customers using the console flow.
- Provide an auditable export accepted by SOC/PCI-style assessors internally.
- Ensure multi-region consistency: the certificate must reflect successful expunge in every data residency zone the tenant uses or clearly indicate partial failures.

Non-goals:
- This scope does not include legal hold workflows (handled in a follow-on ticket).
- Does not change retention policy language, only the orchestration and evidence export for deletion requests.
acceptance_criteria: Console wizard can create a scoped deletion request with filters: data class, date range, and region list.
API endpoint POST /v1/tenant/:id/erase accepts the same payload and returns a request id.
Pipeline emits a signed ZIP containing: human-readable summary, timeline of steps with UTC timestamps, per-shard checksums, and a root SHA256 hash signed by the platform key.
Webhook delivery attempt is retried with exponential backoff and failures are visible in tenant Console UI with actionable retry button.
E2E test demonstrates deletion request completing successfully across two replica zones and produces matching certificates for both zones.
Security review completed and key rotation plan documented in Confluence.
Telemetry: metric erase.requests.success_rate >= 95% in pilot tenants and mean time to complete (median) < 2 hours for small tenants.
Customer-facing documentation and sample webhook verifier library (node/python) published in docs repo.

Design: high-fidelity export summary layout + legal-friendly phrasing
Eng (Orchestration): implement state machine for erase pipeline with idempotency and ordered steps
Eng (Storage): implement per-region expunge handshake and per-shard checksum generation
Eng (Security): implement signing service for hashchain and key rotation endpoints
Console: wizard UI + webhook subscription management and status dashboard
E2E: build test harness to simulate cross-region deletion and compare certificates
Docs: developer guide, webhook verifier samples, and compliance FAQ

discussion: 2026-02-26 - June Park: Kickoff with Compliance and Security. Decided to avoid cryptographic timelines that require third-party notaries; we'll produce signed hashchains using our KMS-backed signing key and expose public certs for customer verification.
2026-03-01 - Ravi Menon: Prototype of pipeline state machine completed (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/erase-orch/pull/134). Needs idempotency keys and stronger retries for the replica sweep step.
2026-03-03 - Priya Shah (Security): Recommended HSM/KMS-backed signing with explicit rotation cadence. Blocker: UAT requires access to staging HSM - security gating in progress.

2026-03-06 - Design review: Export layout accepted with minor edits (Confluence: /display/COM/Erase+Summary+Layout). Action: add 'scope hash' to top-level summary for easier automated matching by customers.

2026-03-09 - Engineering: Added webhook webhook.delivery.metric and admin retry in Console. Integration test flaky in zone eu-west-1; suspected background compaction causing delayed index tombstone application. Mitigation: add a forced index sweep as final step for RTBF flow.

2026-03-11 - PM note: Pilot planning with three customers (two EU, one US). Customers require proof that deletion touches both primary and cold-store replicas. Will run manual end-to-end with engineering before enabling self-serve.
2026-03-12 - Legal: Request to include retained-exception block (if legal hold exists) in the export and a clear 'incomplete due to hold' status. Added as follow-up sub-issue.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full cryptographic notarization (expensive & slow) vs. signed hashchain (fast, auditable). Decided on signed hashchain for 1st release with potential notarization add-on later.
Operational concern: long-running erases could be OOM on control-plane if we keep all state in memory; engineering to persist state to task store and stream events to the audit ledger.
Customer UX: include an estimated completion time window in the wizard using tenant historical throughput; remove precise ETA to avoid SLA commitments.
Metrics to track: erase.request_latency_p50/p95, erase.request_failures_by_reason, webhook.delivery_success_rate, certificate_verification_failures.
